docs.title: CROID
docs.text: The CROID (Crossref Research Object ID) system provides unique, URL-safe identifiers for research objects to track metadata across different systems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A CROID acts as an identifier separate from others like DOIs or ORCIDs, allowing tracking of research objects regardless of metadata changes or missing standards.

docs.title: Create CROID
docs.text:
POST /croid

Links an object's identity (via cro_type, cro_value, system) to a CROID.

Request Body:

{
  "cro_type": "DOI",
  "cro_value": "10.5555/12345678",
  "system": "nauvis"
}

Responses: - 201 Created: New CROID minted. - 200 OK: Existing CROID found (Idempotent). - 400 Bad Request: Missing or invalid parameters.

docs.title: Retrieve Metadata
docs.text:
GET /croid/{croid}

Fetches the metadata associated with a specific CROID.

Response Body:

{
  "cro_type": "DOI",
  "cro_value": "10.5555/12345678",
  "system": "nauvis",
  "croid": "aaaaa12345_aaaaa12345-aaaaa12345",
  "created_at": "2026-05-28T19:04:17Z"
}

Responses: - 200 OK: Success. - 404 Not Found: CROID does not exist.

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text:
• Language: Go 1.25
  • Database: SQLite (using modernc.org/sqlite: a pure-Go, CGO-free driver).
  • Querying: sqlc generates type-safe database access logic.
  • Concurrency: The service is idempotent; concurrent creation requests for the same identity safely return the single existing CROID.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To run the service:

go run main.go --addr :8080 --db croid.sqlite3

To test:

curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"cro_type":"DOI","cro_value":"10.5555/example","system":"nauvis"}' http://localhost:8080/croid
